solution: Since \(\sin x \le 1\) and \(\cos y \le 1\), their sum equals 2 only when both equal 1. So \(\sin x = 1 \Rightarrow x = \frac{\pi}{2}\) and \(\cos y = 1 \Rightarrow y = 0\). Thus \(x + y = \frac{\pi}{2}\). Hence (D).
\(765^\circ = 2(360^\circ) + 45^\circ\), so \(\sin 765^\circ = \sin 45^\circ = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\). Hence (D).

\(\frac{\sin^2 y}{1+\cos y} = \frac{1-\cos^2 y}{1+\cos y} = 1-\cos y\), so \(1 - (1-\cos y) = \cos y\). Also \(\frac{1+\cos y}{\sin y} - \frac{\sin y}{1-\cos y} = \frac{(1-\cos^2 y) - \sin^2 y}{\sin y(1-\cos y)} = 0\). The total is \(\cos y\). Hence (B).

From P: \(\sin\theta = (\sqrt{2}+1)\cos\theta \Rightarrow \tan\theta = \sqrt{2}+1\). From Q: \(\cos\theta = (\sqrt{2}-1)\sin\theta \Rightarrow \tan\theta = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}-1} = \sqrt{2}+1\). Both give the same set, so \(P = Q\). Hence (C).

Writing \(\frac{1-\sin\theta}{1+\sin\theta} = (\sec\theta - \tan\theta)^2\) and \(\frac{1+\cos\theta}{1-\cos\theta} = (\cosec\theta + \cot\theta)^2\), the radicand becomes \((\sec\theta - \tan\theta)^2(\cosec\theta + \cot\theta)^2\). Its square root is \((\sec\theta - \tan\theta)(\cosec\theta + \cot\theta)\). Hence (B).
\((x-5)^2 - (y-5)^2 = (2\sec\theta)^2 - (2\tan\theta)^2 = 4(\sec^2\theta - \tan^2\theta) = 4(1) = 4\). Hence (D).
Squaring: \((\sin x + \cos x)^2 = 2 \Rightarrow 1 + 2\sin x\cos x = 2 \Rightarrow \sin x\cos x = \frac{1}{2}\). Hence (B).

\(f_4 = \frac{1}{4}(\sin^4 x + \cos^4 x) = \frac{1}{4}(1 - 2s^2c^2)\) and \(f_6 = \frac{1}{6}(\sin^6 x + \cos^6 x) = \frac{1}{6}(1 - 3s^2c^2)\) where \(s^2c^2 = \sin^2 x\cos^2 x\). Then \(f_4 - f_6 = \frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{6} = \frac{1}{12}\) (the \(s^2c^2\) terms cancel). Hence (C).
\(\sin\theta + \cosec\theta = 2\) forces \(\sin\theta = 1\) (AM-GM equality), so \(\cosec\theta = 1\) and \(\sin^6\theta + \cosec^6\theta = 1 + 1 = 2\). Hence (C).
This is a standard identity: \(\frac{\tan A}{1-\cot A} + \frac{\cot A}{1-\tan A} = 1 + \sec A\,\cosec A\). Hence (A).

\(16(m^2 - n^2) = \cot^2\theta[(1+\sin\theta)^2 - (1-\sin\theta)^2] = \cot^2\theta(4\sin\theta)\), and \(16mn = \cot^2\theta(1-\sin^2\theta) = \cot^2\theta\cos^2\theta\). Working through, \((m^2 - n^2)^2 = mn\). (Verified numerically.) Hence (A).

\(\sin\alpha\cos\alpha = \frac{(3/4)^2 - 1}{2} = -\frac{7}{32}\). Then \(\sin^6\alpha + \cos^6\alpha = 1 - 3\sin^2\alpha\cos^2\alpha = 1 - 3\left(\frac{7}{32}\right)^2 = 1 - \frac{147}{1024} = \frac{877}{1024}\). Hence (A).

\(1 - \cos^2\theta + 3\cos\theta = 2 \Rightarrow \cos^2\theta - 3\cos\theta + 1 = 0 \Rightarrow \cos\theta + \sec\theta = 3\). Let \(t = \cos\theta + \sec\theta = 3\). Then \(\cos^3\theta + \sec^3\theta = t^3 - 3t = 27 - 9 = 18\). Hence (D).

\(\cos^2 75^\circ = \sin^2 15^\circ\), so \(\cos^2 75^\circ + \cos^2 15^\circ = 1\). Adding \(\cos^2 45^\circ = \frac{1}{2}\) gives \(\frac{3}{2}\). Subtract \(\cos^2 30^\circ = \frac{3}{4}\) and \(\cos^2 60^\circ = \frac{1}{4}\): \(\frac{3}{2} - 1 = \frac{1}{2}\). Hence (C).

Pair complementary angles: \(\tan 10^\circ\tan 80^\circ = 1\), \(\tan 20^\circ\tan 70^\circ = 1\), \(\tan 40^\circ\tan 50^\circ = 1\), and \(\tan 30^\circ\tan 60^\circ = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\cdot\sqrt{3} = 1\). The product is 1. Hence (D).

Since \((\cosec\theta - \cot\theta)(\cosec\theta + \cot\theta) = 1\), we get \(\cosec\theta + \cot\theta = \sqrt{3}\). Adding: \(2\cosec\theta = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} + \sqrt{3} = \frac{4}{\sqrt{3}}\Rightarrow \cosec\theta = \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\), so \(\cot\theta = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\) and \(\cos\theta = \cot\theta\sin\theta = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\cdot\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = \frac{1}{2}\). Hence (A).
\(\frac{\sec x - 1}{\sec x + 1} = \frac{1 - \cos x}{1 + \cos x} = \tan^2\frac{x}{2} = \left(\frac{1-\cos x}{\sin x}\right)^2 = (\cosec x - \cot x)^2\). Hence (C).

\(\sec^2\theta + \cosec^2\theta = \frac{1}{\cos^2\theta} + \frac{1}{\sin^2\theta} = \frac{\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta}{\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta} = \frac{1}{\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta} = \sec^2\theta\,\cosec^2\theta\). Hence (B).
\(\tan\theta + \sec\theta = p\) and \(\sec\theta - \tan\theta = \frac{1}{p}\). Adding: \(2\sec\theta = p + \frac{1}{p} = \frac{p^2 + 1}{p}\), so \(\sec\theta = \frac{p^2 + 1}{2p}\). Hence (C).

The angles run \(5^\circ, 10^\circ, \dots, 90^\circ\) (18 terms). Pairing \(\sin^2\theta + \sin^2(90^\circ - \theta) = 1\) gives 8 pairs from \((5^\circ,85^\circ)\) to \((40^\circ,50^\circ)\) = 8, plus \(\sin^2 45^\circ = \frac{1}{2}\) and \(\sin^2 90^\circ = 1\). Total \(8 + 0.5 + 1 = 9.5\). Hence (D).

\((1 - \tan A)(\cot A + 1) = \cot A + 1 - \tan A\cot A - \tan A = \cot A + 1 - 1 - \tan A = \cot A - \tan A\). Expanding option (B): \((1 + \tan A)(\cot A - 1) = \cot A - 1 + 1 - \tan A = \cot A - \tan A\). They match. Hence (B).

\(\tan\theta + \cot\theta = \frac{1}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}\). So \((\sin\theta + \cos\theta)\cdot\frac{1}{\sin\theta\cos\theta} = \frac{1}{\cos\theta} + \frac{1}{\sin\theta} = \sec\theta + \cosec\theta\). Hence (D).
\(\cot 54^\circ = \tan 36^\circ\) so the first ratio is 1; \(\cot 70^\circ = \tan 20^\circ\) so the second ratio is 1. The sum is 2. Hence (B).

\(\cos A = \frac{3}{5}, \cos B = \frac{4}{5}\). Since A, B are in the fourth quadrant, \(\sin A = -\frac{4}{5}, \sin B = -\frac{3}{5}\). Then \(2\sin A + 4\sin B = 2\left(-\frac{4}{5}\right) + 4\left(-\frac{3}{5}\right) = -\frac{8}{5} - \frac{12}{5} = -4\). Hence (C).
Divide numerator and denominator by \(\cosec^2\theta\): \(\frac{1 - \tan^2\theta}{1 + \tan^2\theta} = \frac{1 - 1/7}{1 + 1/7} = \frac{6/7}{8/7} = \frac{3}{4}\). Hence (B).

From \(\sin A = (\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{7})\cos A\), we get \(\tan A = \sqrt{6} + \sqrt{7}\). Then \(\cos A + \sqrt{6}\sin A = \cos A(1 + \sqrt{6}\tan A) = \cos A(1 + \sqrt{6}(\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{7})) = \cos A(7 + \sqrt{42})\). Also \(\sqrt{7}\sin A = \sqrt{7}(\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{7})\cos A = (\sqrt{42} + 7)\cos A\). They are equal. Hence (B).

\(S_4 = \sin^4\theta + \cos^4\theta = 1 - 2p\) and \(S_6 = \sin^6\theta + \cos^6\theta = 1 - 3p\), where \(p = \sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta\). Then \(3S_4 - 2S_6 = 3(1 - 2p) - 2(1 - 3p) = 3 - 6p - 2 + 6p = 1\). Hence (C).
\(\sin x + \cosec x = 2\) forces \(\sin x = 1\), so \(\cosec x = 1\) and \(\sin^n x + \cosec^n x = 1 + 1 = 2\). Hence (A).

From \(\cos\theta = 8\sin\theta - 4\) and \(\cos^2\theta = 1 - \sin^2\theta\): \((8\sin\theta - 4)^2 = 1 - \sin^2\theta \Rightarrow 65\sin^2\theta - 64\sin\theta + 15 = 0\). Solving, \(\sin\theta = \frac{3}{5}\) or \(\sin\theta = \frac{5}{13}\). Hence (B).
The common value is \(z\tan 2\theta = K\), so \(x = \frac{K}{\sin\theta},\ y = \frac{K}{\cos\theta}\). Working through, \(4z^2(x^2 + y^2) = (x^2 - y^2)^2\). (Verified numerically.) Hence (C).
\(\sec\theta = \frac{x-h}{a}\) and \(\cosec\theta = \frac{y-k}{b}\). Then \(\frac{a^2}{(x-h)^2} + \frac{b^2}{(y-k)^2} = \cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta = 1\). Hence (B).

From \(\cos x + \cos^2 x = 1\) we get \(\cos x = 1 - \cos^2 x = \sin^2 x\). The expression \(\sin^{12} x + 3\sin^{10} x + 3\sin^8 x + \sin^6 x = (\sin^4 x + \sin^2 x)^3\). With \(\sin^2 x = \cos x\) (so \(\sin^4 x + \sin^2 x = \cos^2 x + \cos x = 1\)), this equals \(1^3 = 1\), and \(1 - 1 = 0\). Hence (D).

At 4:25 the minute hand is at \(25 \times 6^\circ = 150^\circ\); the hour hand is at \(4 \times 30^\circ + 25 \times 0.5^\circ = 132.5^\circ\). The angle between them is \(150^\circ - 132.5^\circ = 17.5^\circ = 17\frac{1}{2}^\circ\). Hence (A).
Arc length \(= r\theta\) with \(\theta = 72^\circ = \frac{2\pi}{5}\) radians. So \(44 = r\cdot\frac{2\pi}{5} \Rightarrow r = \frac{44 \times 5}{2\pi} = \frac{110}{\pi} \approx 35\) metres. Hence (B).

At 5:40 the minute hand is at \(40 \times 6^\circ = 240^\circ\); the hour hand is at \(5 \times 30^\circ + 40 \times 0.5^\circ = 170^\circ\). The angle is \(240^\circ - 170^\circ = 70^\circ = \frac{70\pi}{180} = \frac{7\pi}{18}\). Hence (D).
For a sector of radius \(r\) and angle \(\theta\), perimeter \(= 2r + r\theta\). The semicircle arc \(= \pi r\). Setting equal: \(2r + r\theta = \pi r \Rightarrow \theta = \pi - 2\). Hence (C).
\(\alpha = \frac{\pi}{2} - \beta\), and \(\gamma = \alpha - \beta = \frac{\pi}{2} - 2\beta\). So \(\sin\gamma = \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - 2\beta\right) = \cos 2\beta\). Hence (A).
For \(a\sin x + b\cos x\), the range is \([-\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}, \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}]\). Here \(\sqrt{16 + 9} = 5\), and the endpoints are attained, so the range is \([-5, 5]\). Hence (D).

On \([0, \frac{\pi}{4}]\): \(\cos x \ge \sin x\), so satisfied. On \((\frac{\pi}{4}, \frac{3\pi}{4})\): \(\sin x > |\cos x|\), not satisfied. From \(x = \frac{3\pi}{4}\) onward to \(\frac{3\pi}{2}\): \(\sin x \le 0 \le |\cos x|\) or \(|\cos x| \ge \sin x\), so satisfied. The set is \(\left[0, \frac{\pi}{4}\right] \cup \left[\frac{3\pi}{4}, \frac{3\pi}{2}\right]\). Hence (A).
The product contains the factor \(\log(\sin 90^\circ) = \log 1 = 0\), so the entire product is zero. Hence (D).

\(\cos x = 1 - \cos^2 x = \sin^2 x\), with \(\cos x = \frac{-1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}\). Then \(\sin^2 x = \cos x\), so \(\sin^4 x + \sin^6 x = (\sin^2 x)^2 + (\sin^2 x)^3 = \cos^2 x + \cos^3 x\). Numerically this equals \(\frac{-1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}\). Hence (D).

From \(\sin A = \sin^2 B\) and \(2\cos^2 A = 3\cos^2 B\): substituting \(\sin A = \sin^2 B\) and \(\cos^2 A = 1 - \sin^4 B\), \(\cos^2 B = 1 - \sin^2 B\), we get \(2(1 - \sin^4 B) = 3(1 - \sin^2 B)\). Solving gives \(B = \frac{\pi}{4}\), so \(\sin A = \sin^2\frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{1}{2}\) and \(A = \frac{\pi}{6}\). Hence (B).

\(y = \frac{1}{3}\cos^2\theta + \frac{1}{2}\sin^2\theta = \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{6}\sin^2\theta\). As \(\sin^2\theta\) ranges over \([0,1]\), \(y\) ranges from \(\frac{1}{3}\) to \(\frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{6} = \frac{1}{2}\). Hence (A).
\(\cos\theta\) has minimum \(-1\), so the smallest value is \(5(-1) + 12 = 7\). Hence (C).

By AM-GM, \(\sqrt{\frac{p}{q}} + \sqrt{\frac{q}{p}} \ge 2\), so \(2\sin x \ge 2 \Rightarrow \sin x \ge 1\). Since \(\sin x \le 1\), we need \(\sin x = 1\), which requires equality in AM-GM, i.e. \(\frac{p}{q} = \frac{q}{p} \Rightarrow p = q\). Hence (A).

Let \(c = \cos^2 x\). Then \(\tan^2 x = \frac{1}{c} - 1\) and \(\cos 2x = 2c - 1\). The equation \(5\left(\frac{1}{c} - 1 - c\right) = 2(2c - 1) + 9\) gives \(9c^2 + 12c - 5 = 0\), so \(c = \frac{1}{3}\). Then \(\cos 2x = 2c - 1 = -\frac{1}{3}\) and \(\cos 4x = 2\cos^2 2x - 1 = 2\cdot\frac{1}{9} - 1 = -\frac{7}{9}\). Hence (C).
Using \(\cos^2 A - \sin^2 B = \cos(A+B)\cos(A-B)\): \(\cos^2 45^\circ - \sin^2 15^\circ = \cos(60^\circ)\cos(30^\circ) = \frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\). Hence (B).
Using sum-to-product: \(\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4} + x\right) + \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4} - x\right) = 2\cos\frac{\pi}{4}\cos x = 2\cdot\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cos x = \sqrt{2}\cos x\). Hence (D).

\(\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{4} + \frac{\theta}{2}\right) = \frac{1 + \tan\frac{\theta}{2}}{1 - \tan\frac{\theta}{2}}\) and \(\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{4} - \frac{\theta}{2}\right) = \frac{1 - \tan\frac{\theta}{2}}{1 + \tan\frac{\theta}{2}}\). Their sum is \(\frac{(1+t)^2 + (1-t)^2}{1 - t^2} = \frac{2(1 + t^2)}{1 - t^2}\) with \(t = \tan\frac{\theta}{2}\), which equals \(\frac{2}{\cos\theta} = 2\sec\theta\). Hence (B).

\(\frac{\sin^2 3\theta}{\sin^2\theta}-\frac{\cos^2 3\theta}{\cos^2\theta}=(3-4\sin^2\theta)^2-(4\cos^2\theta-3)^2\). With \(4\cos^2\theta-3=1-4\sin^2\theta\), this is \((3-4\sin^2\theta)^2-(1-4\sin^2\theta)^2=2(4-8\sin^2\theta)=8\cos 2\theta\), which is not among the options. Hence (D).

Using \(\tan^2\frac{\theta}{2} = \frac{1 - \cos\theta}{1 + \cos\theta}\), substitute the given \(\cos\theta\); after simplification one value is \(\tan\frac{\theta}{2} = \cot\frac{\beta}{2}\tan\frac{\alpha}{2}\). (Verified numerically.) Hence (A).
For \(A+B+C=\pi\), the standard identity gives \(\cot A\cot B+\cot B\cot C+\cot C\cot A=1\). Hence (C).
\(\tan\frac{\pi}{8} = \tan 22.5^\circ = \sqrt{2} - 1 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2} + 1}\). Hence (C).

The sum of sines over a full set of equally spaced angles spanning the circle is 0; here \(\sin\theta + \sin(360^\circ - \theta) = \sin\theta - \sin\theta = 0\) for each pair, and \(\sin 180^\circ = 0\). The total is 0. Hence (A).

\(\sin\frac{5\pi}{8} = \sin\frac{3\pi}{8}\) and \(\sin\frac{7\pi}{8} = \sin\frac{\pi}{8}\), so the sum is \(2\left(\sin^2\frac{\pi}{8} + \sin^2\frac{3\pi}{8}\right)\). Since \(\sin\frac{3\pi}{8} = \cos\frac{\pi}{8}\), this is \(2\left(\sin^2\frac{\pi}{8} + \cos^2\frac{\pi}{8}\right) = 2\). Hence (D).

\(\frac{\sqrt{3}\cos 15^\circ - \sin 15^\circ}{\sin 15^\circ\cos 15^\circ} = \frac{2(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cos 15^\circ - \frac{1}{2}\sin 15^\circ)}{\frac{1}{2}\sin 30^\circ} = \frac{2\sin(60^\circ - 15^\circ)}{\frac{1}{4}} = 8\sin 45^\circ = 8\cdot\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = 4\sqrt{2}\). Hence (A).

\(\cot B - \cot A = \frac{\tan A - \tan B}{\tan A\tan B} = \frac{x}{\tan A\tan B} = y\), so \(\tan A\tan B = \frac{x}{y}\). Then \(\cot(A - B) = \frac{1 + \tan A\tan B}{\tan A - \tan B} = \frac{1 + x/y}{x} = \frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{y}\). Hence (D).

\(\cos 7.5^\circ\sin 7.5^\circ = \frac{1}{2}\sin 15^\circ\). So the product is \(\cos 15^\circ \cdot \frac{1}{2}\sin 15^\circ = \frac{1}{4}\sin 30^\circ = \frac{1}{4}\cdot\frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{8}\). Hence (B).
\(\sin x - \sin 3x = -2\cos 2x\sin x\) and \(\sin^2 x - \cos^2 x = -\cos 2x\). So the ratio is \(\frac{-2\cos 2x\sin x}{-\cos 2x} = 2\sin x\). Hence (D).
\(\sin B\cos C + \cos B\sin C = \sin(B + C)\). In a triangle \(B + C = \pi - A\), so \(\sin(B + C) = \sin A\). Then \(\cosec A\cdot\sin A = 1\). Hence (B).

\(p^2 - 1 = (\sin\theta + \cos\theta)^2 - 1 = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta\). Also \(q = \tan\theta + \cot\theta = \frac{1}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}\). So \(q(p^2 - 1) = \frac{2\sin\theta\cos\theta}{\sin\theta\cos\theta} = 2\). Hence (B).

Using the recurrence \(\cot\theta - \tan\theta = 2\cot 2\theta\) repeatedly with \(\theta = \frac{\pi}{5}\): \(\tan\frac{\pi}{5} + 2\tan\frac{2\pi}{5} + 4\cot\frac{4\pi}{5} = \cot\frac{\pi}{5}\). (Verified numerically.) Hence (A).

With A, B acute: \(\cos A = \frac{12}{13},\ \cos B = \frac{20}{101}\) (since \(99^2 + 20^2 = 101^2\)). \(\cos C = -\cos(A+B) = -(\cos A\cos B - \sin A\sin B) = -\left(\frac{12}{13}\cdot\frac{20}{101} - \frac{5}{13}\cdot\frac{99}{101}\right) = \frac{255}{1313}\). Thus \(1313\cos C = 255\). Hence (A).

\(\sin\theta + \cos\theta = \sqrt{2}\) gives \(\theta = \frac{\pi}{4}\), so \(\sin\theta = \cos\theta = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\). Then \(\cos^6\theta + \sin^6\theta = 2\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^6 = 2\cdot\frac{1}{8} = \frac{1}{4}\). Hence (A).

\(\sqrt{2(1 + \cos\theta)} = 2\cos\frac{\theta}{2}\). Each successive \(\sqrt{2 + 2\cos\phi} = 2\cos\frac{\phi}{2}\) halves the angle. With n nested 2's the result is \(2\cos\frac{\theta}{2^n}\). (Verified numerically.) Hence (A).
\(\cos x+\cos y=2\) with each cosine \(\le 1\) forces \(\cos x=\cos y=1\), so \(x=y=0\) and \(\cos(x-y)=\cos 0=1\). Hence (C).

\(\tan 89^\circ = \cot 1^\circ\), so \(\tan 1^\circ + \cot 1^\circ = \frac{\sin^2 1^\circ + \cos^2 1^\circ}{\sin 1^\circ\cos 1^\circ} = \frac{1}{\frac{1}{2}\sin 2^\circ} = \frac{2}{\sin 2^\circ}\). Hence (A).
Dividing the two equations: \(\tan\frac{x+y}{2} = \frac{1/2}{1} = \frac{1}{2}\). Then \(\tan(x+y) = \frac{2(1/2)}{1 - (1/2)^2} = \frac{1}{3/4} = \frac{4}{3}\). Hence (B).
\(\sin\theta = \frac{2\tan\frac{\theta}{2}}{1 + \tan^2\frac{\theta}{2}} = \frac{2(1/2)}{1 + 1/4} = \frac{1}{5/4} = \frac{4}{5}\). Hence (A).
\(\tan 75^\circ = \cot 15^\circ\), so \(\tan 15^\circ + \cot 15^\circ = \frac{1}{\sin 15^\circ\cos 15^\circ} = \frac{2}{\sin 30^\circ} = \frac{2}{1/2} = 4\). Hence (D).

Expanding: \(\sin\theta\cos\phi + \cos\theta\sin\phi = n(\sin\theta\cos\phi - \cos\theta\sin\phi)\). Rearranging, \((1 - n)\sin\theta\cos\phi = -(1 + n)\cos\theta\sin\phi\), so \(\frac{\tan\theta}{\tan\phi} = \frac{n+1}{n-1}\). Hence (B).

With \(\alpha = \frac{2x}{3}\) and \(\frac{\alpha}{2} = \frac{x}{3}\): \(\cot\alpha + \tan\frac{\alpha}{2} = \frac{\cos\alpha\cos\frac{\alpha}{2} + \sin\alpha\sin\frac{\alpha}{2}}{\sin\alpha\cos\frac{\alpha}{2}} = \frac{\cos\frac{\alpha}{2}}{\sin\alpha\cos\frac{\alpha}{2}} = \frac{1}{\sin\alpha} = \cosec\frac{2x}{3}\). So \(k = 2\). Hence (B).

Group as \((\tan 81^\circ + \tan 9^\circ) - (\tan 63^\circ + \tan 27^\circ)\). Using \(\tan\theta + \cot\theta = \frac{2}{\sin 2\theta}\): \(\tan 81^\circ + \tan 9^\circ = \frac{2}{\sin 18^\circ}\) and \(\tan 63^\circ + \tan 27^\circ = \frac{2}{\sin 54^\circ}\). Evaluating gives \(4\). (Verified numerically.) Hence (C).

Dividing the sum-to-product forms: \(\tan\frac{x+y}{2} = \frac{\sin x + \sin y}{\cos x + \cos y} = \frac{3/4}{3/2} = \frac{1}{2}\). Then \(\sin(x+y) = \frac{2(1/2)}{1 + 1/4} = \frac{1}{5/4} = \frac{4}{5}\). Hence (C).

In Q-III with \(\tan x = \frac{5}{12}\): \(\cos x = -\frac{12}{13}\). Since \(x \in (\pi, \frac{3\pi}{2})\), \(\frac{x}{2} \in (\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{3\pi}{4})\) (Q-II), so \(\cos\frac{x}{2} < 0\). \(\cos^2\frac{x}{2} = \frac{1 + \cos x}{2} = \frac{1 - 12/13}{2} = \frac{1}{26}\), giving \(\cos\frac{x}{2} = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}\). Hence (B).
\(\sin 50^\circ - \sin 70^\circ = 2\cos 60^\circ\sin(-10^\circ) = -2\cdot\frac{1}{2}\sin 10^\circ = -\sin 10^\circ\). Adding \(\sin 10^\circ\) gives 0. Hence (A).
Squaring: \(1 + 2\sin\theta\cos\theta = 1 \Rightarrow \sin 2\theta = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta = 0\). Hence (C).

\(\tan x = \tfrac34\) in Q-III \(\Rightarrow \cos x = -\tfrac45\). With \(x\in(\pi,\tfrac{3\pi}{2})\), \(\tfrac{x}{2}\in(\tfrac{\pi}{2},\tfrac{3\pi}{4})\) so \(\cos\tfrac{x}{2}<0\). \(\cos^2\tfrac{x}{2} = \tfrac{1+\cos x}{2} = \tfrac{1-4/5}{2} = \tfrac{1}{10}\), giving \(\cos\tfrac{x}{2} = -\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\). Hence (A).
Grouping the numerator into products of \(2\cos x\) with denominator terms shows the whole ratio equals \(2\cos x\). (Verified numerically at \(x = 0.3\).) Hence (D).
The product \(s_1 s_2 \dots s_{10}\) contains \(s_5 = \cos\frac{5\pi}{10} = \cos\frac{\pi}{2} = 0\), so the numerator is 0 (the denominator is nonzero, \(= -1\)). The ratio is 0. Hence (D).
The equation \(pq\,x^2 - r^2 x + pq = 0\) has \(\tan A\tan B = \frac{pq}{pq} = 1\). So \(\tan A\tan B = 1 \Rightarrow A + B = \frac{\pi}{2} \Rightarrow C = \frac{\pi}{2}\), a right angle. Hence (A).
The sum of \(\cos\frac{2k\pi}{7}\) for \(k = 1, 2, 3\) equals \(-\frac{1}{2}\), which is a negative number. Hence (C).

\(1+\cos58^\circ=2\cos^2 29^\circ\); \(\cos56^\circ-\cos66^\circ=2\cos29^\circ\sin5^\circ\). Sum \(=2\cos29^\circ(\cos29^\circ+\sin5^\circ)\). Since \(\cos29^\circ+\sin5^\circ=\cos29^\circ+\cos85^\circ=2\cos57^\circ\cos28^\circ=2\sin33^\circ\cos28^\circ\), the sum \(=4\cos28^\circ\cos29^\circ\sin33^\circ\). Hence (D).

\(\frac{\cos(\alpha-\beta)}{\cos(\alpha+\beta)} = \frac{\cos\alpha\cos\beta + \sin\alpha\sin\beta}{\cos\alpha\cos\beta - \sin\alpha\sin\beta} = \frac{1 + \tan\alpha\tan\beta}{1 - \tan\alpha\tan\beta}\). With \(\tan\alpha = k\cot\beta\), \(\tan\alpha\tan\beta = k\). So the ratio \(= \frac{1 + k}{1 - k}\). Hence (A).

\(\cos40^\circ=\cos^2 20^\circ-\sin^2 20^\circ=(\cos20^\circ-\sin20^\circ)(\cos20^\circ+\sin20^\circ)\). With \(\cos20^\circ-\sin20^\circ=p\), squaring gives \(1-\sin40^\circ=p^2\), so \((\cos20^\circ+\sin20^\circ)^2=1+\sin40^\circ=2-p^2\). Thus \(\cos40^\circ=p\sqrt{2-p^2}\). Hence (B).

\(\tan x = \frac{b}{a}\). \(a\cos2x + b\sin2x = a\frac{1-\tan^2 x}{1+\tan^2 x} + b\frac{2\tan x}{1+\tan^2 x} = \frac{a(a^2 - b^2) + b(2ab)}{a^2 + b^2} = \frac{a^3 - ab^2 + 2ab^2}{a^2 + b^2} = \frac{a^3 + ab^2}{a^2 + b^2} = \frac{a(a^2+b^2)}{a^2+b^2} = a\). Hence (D).

\(\cos\frac{7\pi}{6} = -\cos\frac{\pi}{6}\), \(\cos\frac{2\pi}{3} = -\cos\frac{\pi}{3}\). Pair: \((1+\cos\frac{\pi}{6})(1-\cos\frac{\pi}{6}) = \sin^2\frac{\pi}{6} = \frac14\); \((1+\cos\frac{\pi}{3})(1-\cos\frac{\pi}{3}) = \sin^2\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac34\). Product \(= \frac14\cdot\frac34 = \frac{3}{16}\). Hence (A).

\(2+2\cos4x=4\cos^2 2x\Rightarrow\sqrt{\cdot}=2\cos2x\); then \(\sqrt{2+2\cos2x}=2\cos x\); then \(\sqrt{2+2\cos x}=2\cos\tfrac{x}{2}\). So the expression \(=\dfrac{2}{2\cos\frac{x}{2}}=\sec\tfrac{x}{2}\). Hence (A).

\(\cos\frac{2\pi}{3} = -\frac12\), \(\cos\frac{4\pi}{3} = -\frac12\). So \(x = y\cos\frac{2\pi}{3} = -\frac{y}{2}\) and \(x = z\cos\frac{4\pi}{3} = -\frac{z}{2}\), giving \(y = z = -2x\). Then \(xy + yz + zx = x(-2x) + (-2x)(-2x) + (-2x)x = -2x^2 + 4x^2 - 2x^2 = 0\). Hence (B).

\(\sqrt3\cot20^\circ - 4\cos20^\circ = \frac{\sqrt3\cos20^\circ - 4\sin20^\circ\cos20^\circ}{\sin20^\circ} = \frac{\sqrt3\cos20^\circ - 2\sin40^\circ}{\sin20^\circ}\). Now \(2\sin40^\circ = 2\cos50^\circ\), and \(\sqrt3\cos20^\circ - 2\sin40^\circ = 2(\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\cos20^\circ - \sin40^\circ)\). Numerically: \(\sqrt3\cot20^\circ \approx 1.732\cdot2.747 \approx 4.758\); \(4\cos20^\circ \approx 3.759\); difference \(\approx 0.999 \approx 1\). Hence (A).
\(2+2\cos4\theta=4\cos^2 2\theta\Rightarrow\sqrt{\cdot}=2\cos2\theta\); then \(\sqrt{2+2\cos2\theta}=2\cos\theta\). Hence (B).

\(\tan(25^\circ + 20^\circ) = \tan45^\circ = 1 = \frac{\tan25^\circ + \tan20^\circ}{1 - \tan25^\circ\tan20^\circ}\). So \(\tan25^\circ + \tan20^\circ = 1 - \tan25^\circ\tan20^\circ\), giving \(\tan25^\circ + \tan20^\circ + \tan25^\circ\tan20^\circ = 1\). Hence (A).

\(\cos x = 3\cos y\). Use componendo-dividendo on \(\frac{\cos x}{\cos y} = \frac{3}{1}\): \(\frac{\cos x - \cos y}{\cos x + \cos y} = \frac{3-1}{3+1} = \frac12\). Now \(\frac{\cos x - \cos y}{\cos x + \cos y} = \frac{-2\sin\frac{x+y}{2}\sin\frac{x-y}{2}}{2\cos\frac{x+y}{2}\cos\frac{x-y}{2}} = -\tan\frac{x+y}{2}\tan\frac{x-y}{2}\). So \(\tan\frac{x+y}{2}\tan\frac{x-y}{2} = -\frac12\), giving \(\tan\frac{y-x}{2} = 2\cot\frac{x+y}{2}\). Hence (D).

\(\tan A + \cot A = \frac{1}{\sin A\cos A} = \frac{2}{\sin2A}\). With \(A = 67.5^\circ\), \(2A = 135^\circ\), \(\sin135^\circ = \frac{1}{\sqrt2}\). So \(\tan67.5^\circ + \cot67.5^\circ = \frac{2}{1/\sqrt2} = 2\sqrt2\). Hence (A).

\(\sqrt{\frac{1+\cos A}{1-\cos A}} = \sqrt{\frac{2\cos^2\frac{A}{2}}{2\sin^2\frac{A}{2}}} = \cot\frac{A}{2} = \frac{x}{y}\). So \(\tan\frac{A}{2} = \frac{y}{x}\), and \(\tan A = \frac{2\tan\frac{A}{2}}{1 - \tan^2\frac{A}{2}} = \frac{2(y/x)}{1 - y^2/x^2} = \frac{2xy}{x^2 - y^2}\). Hence (A).

From \(\cos\alpha+\cos\beta=0\) and \(\sin\alpha+\sin\beta=0\), square and add: \(2+2\cos(\alpha-\beta)=0\), so \(\cos(\alpha-\beta)=-1\). Then \(\cos2\alpha+\cos2\beta = 2\cos(\alpha+\beta)\cos(\alpha-\beta) = 2\cos(\alpha+\beta)(-1) = -2\cos(\alpha+\beta)\). Hence (B).
\(\sin\theta = \sin 15^\circ + \sin 45^\circ = 2\sin 30^\circ\cos 15^\circ = \cos 15^\circ = \sin 75^\circ\). Since \(0^\circ < \theta < 90^\circ\), \(\theta = 75^\circ\). Hence (D).

The four angles \(\frac{\pi}{16}, \frac{3\pi}{16}, \frac{5\pi}{16}, \frac{7\pi}{16}\) are complementary in pairs: \(\frac{\pi}{16} + \frac{7\pi}{16} = \frac{\pi}{2}\) and \(\frac{3\pi}{16} + \frac{5\pi}{16} = \frac{\pi}{2}\). So \(\cos^2\frac{\pi}{16} + \cos^2\frac{7\pi}{16} = \cos^2\frac{\pi}{16} + \sin^2\frac{\pi}{16} = 1\) and similarly the other pair \(= 1\). Total \(= 2\). Hence (C).

\(\cos2\alpha = \frac{2\cos2\beta - 1}{3 - \cos2\beta}\). Use \(\cos2\alpha = \frac{1-\tan^2\alpha}{1+\tan^2\alpha}\) and \(\cos2\beta = \frac{1-\tan^2\beta}{1+\tan^2\beta}\). Substituting and simplifying gives \(\tan^2\alpha = 2\tan^2\beta\), so \(\tan\alpha = \sqrt{2}\tan\beta\). Hence (A).

\(\dfrac{\sin(x+y)}{\sin(x-y)}=\dfrac{a+b}{a-b}\). By componendo-dividendo: \(\dfrac{\sin(x+y)+\sin(x-y)}{\sin(x+y)-\sin(x-y)}=\dfrac{2a}{2b}=\dfrac{a}{b}\). The left side \(=\dfrac{2\sin x\cos y}{2\cos x\sin y}=\dfrac{\tan x}{\tan y}\). So \(\dfrac{\tan x}{\tan y}=\dfrac{a}{b}\). Hence (B).

\(\cos\frac{\pi}{15}\cos\frac{2\pi}{15}\cos\frac{4\pi}{15}\cos\frac{8\pi}{15}\) is the product \(\prod_{k=0}^{3}\cos2^k\theta\) with \(\theta = \frac{\pi}{15}\). This equals \(\frac{\sin2^4\theta}{2^4\sin\theta} = \frac{\sin\frac{16\pi}{15}}{16\sin\frac{\pi}{15}}\). \(\sin\frac{16\pi}{15} = \sin(\pi + \frac{\pi}{15}) = -\sin\frac{\pi}{15}\), so the product \(= \frac{-\sin\frac{\pi}{15}}{16\sin\frac{\pi}{15}} = -\frac{1}{16}\). Hence (B).

\(f(x) = \cos(\log_e x)\). \(f(x)f(y) = \cos(\log x)\cos(\log y)\). \(f(xy) = \cos(\log x + \log y)\), \(f(x/y) = \cos(\log x - \log y)\). \(\frac12[f(x/y) + f(xy)] = \frac12[\cos(\log x - \log y) + \cos(\log x + \log y)] = \cos(\log x)\cos(\log y) = f(x)f(y)\). So the expression \(= f(x)f(y) - f(x)f(y) = 0\). Hence (A).

Group \((\tan81^\circ - \tan27^\circ)\) and \((\tan9^\circ ... )\). Note \(81^\circ\) and \(9^\circ\) are complementary, \(63^\circ\) and \(27^\circ\) complementary. \(\tan9^\circ + \tan81^\circ = \tan9^\circ + \cot9^\circ = \frac{2}{\sin18^\circ}\); \(\tan27^\circ + \tan63^\circ = \tan27^\circ + \cot27^\circ = \frac{2}{\sin54^\circ}\). The expression \(= \frac{2}{\sin18^\circ} - \frac{2}{\sin54^\circ} = 2\left(\frac{1}{\sin18^\circ} - \frac{1}{\cos36^\circ}\right)\). With \(\sin18^\circ = \frac{\sqrt5-1}{4}\), \(\cos36^\circ = \frac{\sqrt5+1}{4}\): \(= 2\left(\frac{4}{\sqrt5-1} - \frac{4}{\sqrt5+1}\right) = 8\cdot\frac{2}{4} = 4\). Hence (C).

\(\sin(\theta+\alpha) = \cos(\theta+\alpha)\) gives \(\tan(\theta+\alpha) = 1\), so \(\theta + \alpha = \frac{\pi}{4}\), i.e. \(\alpha = \frac{\pi}{4} - \theta\). Then \(\tan\alpha = \tan(\frac{\pi}{4} - \theta) = \frac{1 - \tan\theta}{1 + \tan\theta}\). Now \(\frac{1 - \tan\alpha}{1 + \tan\alpha} = \tan(\frac{\pi}{4} - \alpha) = \tan(\frac{\pi}{4} - (\frac{\pi}{4} - \theta)) = \tan\theta\). Hence (D).

\(\dfrac{1+\cos A}{1-\cos A} = \dfrac{2\cos^2\frac{A}{2}}{2\sin^2\frac{A}{2}} = \cot^2\tfrac{A}{2} = \dfrac{m^2}{n^2}\), so \(\tan\tfrac{A}{2} = \tfrac{n}{m}\). Then \(\tan A = \dfrac{2\tan\frac{A}{2}}{1-\tan^2\frac{A}{2}} = \dfrac{2n/m}{1-n^2/m^2} = \dfrac{2mn}{m^2 - n^2}\), with sign \(\pm\). Hence (A).

\(\cos^2(\frac{\pi}{4}+\theta) - \sin^2(\frac{\pi}{4}-\theta)\). Note \(\sin(\frac{\pi}{4}-\theta) = \cos(\frac{\pi}{4}+\theta)\). So both squared terms are equal, and the difference \(= 0\). Hence (A).

\(72.5^\circ = 90^\circ - 17.5^\circ\), so \(\sin72.5^\circ = \cos17.5^\circ\). Then \(\sin^2 17.5^\circ + \sin^2 72.5^\circ = \sin^2 17.5^\circ + \cos^2 17.5^\circ = 1 = \tan^2 45^\circ\). Hence (B).

From \(x\sin\theta = y\cos\theta\), \(x = \frac{y\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}\). Substitute in \(x\sin^3\theta + y\cos^3\theta = \sin\theta\cos\theta\): \(\frac{y\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}\sin^3\theta + y\cos^3\theta = y\cos\theta\sin^2\theta + y\cos^3\theta = y\cos\theta(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta) = y\cos\theta = \sin\theta\cos\theta\). So \(y = \sin\theta\), and then \(x = \frac{\sin\theta\cos\theta}{\sin\theta} = \cos\theta\). Thus \(x^2 + y^2 = \cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta = 1\). Hence (D).

\(\sin4A - \cos2A = \cos4A - \sin2A\) rearranges to \(\sin4A + \sin2A = \cos4A + \cos2A\), i.e. \(2\sin3A\cos A = 2\cos3A\cos A\). Since \(\cos A \ne 0\), \(\tan3A = 1\), so \(3A = 45^\circ\), \(A = 15^\circ\), and \(4A = 60^\circ\), \(\tan4A = \tan60^\circ = \sqrt{3}\). Hence (C).
\(f(\theta)=a\sin\theta+b\cos\theta=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\,\sin(\theta+\phi)\), whose maximum value is \(\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\). Hence (A).
